title: The roofline
hints: Arithmetic intensity is `flops /. nbytes`: how many operations each byte you move pays for.
Memory can deliver `bandwidth` GB per second, so it can feed at most `bandwidth *. intensity` GFLOP/s.
Take the smaller of that and `peak`: `Float.min`.

answer.explain: This is the roofline model. For low intensity (an elementwise add does about 1 operation per 12 bytes) memory is the limit, and a faster processor doesn't help. For high intensity (a big matmul reuses every number many times) compute is the limit. The first sample does 2 operations per byte: 20 GB/s times 2 is 40 GFLOP/s, under the 100 peak, so memory wins.
